## Root Cause Analysis: HighErrorRate — shop/frontend

### CONFIRMED — Root cause identified with direct evidence

**Symptom confirmed active:** `frontend` nginx access logs show repeated 500s on `/api/items`, e.g.:
```
20:29:05 "GET /api/items" 500 34
20:29:15 "GET /api/items" 500 34
20:29:25 "GET /api/items" 500 34
20:29:45 "GET /api/items" 500 34
...
```
Roughly 1 in 3 requests fail — consistent with the alert's reported 31% 5xx rate.

**Mechanism (traced outside-in):**
1. `frontend` proxies `/api/` to upstream `http://10.96.149.117:8080` → Service `api` in namespace `shop`.
2. Service `api` selector is `{app: api}` (confirmed via `kubectl get svc api -o yaml`).
3. `kubectl get endpoints api` shows **3** backing pods: `10.244.1.37`, `10.244.1.40`, `10.244.2.48` — but Deployment `api` only has **2** replicas (`10.244.1.37`, `10.244.2.48`).
4. The 3rd endpoint, `10.244.1.40`, belongs to pod `shop-api-69f6fc5964-jhzz8`, from a **separate Deployment `shop-api`**. Its pod template carries labels `app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api` — the `app: api` label is a collision that causes it to be picked up by the production `api` Service's selector even though it's an unrelated/different service.
5. `shop-api`'s code (`configmap/shop-api`, "shop-api 0.9.3") runs `os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]` on every `/items` request. No `DATABASE_URL` env var or Secret exists anywhere in the namespace (`kubectl get secrets -n shop` → empty), so **every single request to this pod throws `KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL'`** and returns HTTP 500 (confirmed in pod logs — the traceback repeats on every `/items` call, 100% failure rate for that pod).
6. Net effect: 1 of the 3 load-balanced endpoints behind `api` fails 100% of the time → ~33% error rate at the Service level, matching the alert's 31% exactly.

**Ruled out:**
- Redis connectivity: both legitimate `api` pods logged `connected to redis at redis:6379` and serve `/items` 200 consistently — no redis errors in their logs.
- Node/resource exhaustion: all 3 nodes `Ready`; `kubectl top pods` shows negligible CPU/memory (1-3m CPU, <15Mi memory) across the namespace — not a capacity issue.
- Frontend/nginx misconfiguration: nginx correctly proxies to the right upstream; the 502s seen at pod startup (connection refused) were transient during initial scheduling (20:28:57) and are unrelated to the ongoing 500s.

**Timing:** `shop-api` Deployment was created at 20:29:03, 9s after the core stack (`api`, `frontend`, `redis`) came up at 20:28:54 — this is a newly introduced, incompletely-configured service whose label collision is the proximate trigger for the alert.

### VALIDATED FIXES

```text
VALIDATED FIXES:
1. Immediately stop shop-api from serving production "api" traffic: kubectl scale deployment shop-api -n shop --replicas=0
   Validated by: `kubectl get deployment shop-api -o yaml` → replicas=1, readyReplicas=1, confirmed only consumer of its traffic is the accidental inclusion in the `api` Service endpoints (no other Service selects it); `kubectl get secrets -n shop` → empty, confirming shop-api is not production-ready (missing required DATABASE_URL) and safe to pause.
   Risk: low | Undo: kubectl scale deployment shop-api -n shop --replicas=1

2. Permanent fix - remove the colliding `app: api` label so shop-api is never selected by the `api` Service: requires recreating/reapplying the shop-api Deployment with selector/template labels changed to e.g. `app: shop-api` only (Deployment selector is immutable, so this needs delete+reapply, not a patch).
   Validated by: `kubectl get svc api -o yaml` → selector is exactly `{app: api}` with no other distinguishing match; `kubectl get deployment shop-api -o yaml` → selector/template both include `app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api`. Removing `app: api` from both fields would exclude it from the `api` Service's endpoint pool.
   Risk: low (isolated to shop-api object) | Undo: reapply prior manifest with `app: api` label restored
```

Fix #1 is the minimum change to restore the frontend error rate to 0% right now. Fix #2 is the structural correction so this doesn't recur when shop-api is reintroduced — it should not ship with the `app: api` label until it's a validated replacement with its own `DATABASE_URL` configured and intentionally wired into the `api` Service.

I'm saving this pattern to memory since the mechanism (label collision pulling an unrelated/broken deployment into a Service's endpoint pool) is non-obvious and likely to recur with other services in this cluster.

streamingThoughts.content: Hypothesis confirmed via direct evidence. Let me verify the deployment specs to pin down exactly how the mislabeled pod got selected and whether DATABASE_URL was ever set.

Root Cause Analysis: HighErrorRate — shop/frontend

CONFIRMED — Root cause identified with direct evidence

Symptom confirmed active: frontend nginx access logs show repeated 500s on /api/items, e.g.:
``
20:29:05 "GET /api/items" 500 34
20:29:15 "GET /api/items" 500 34
20:29:25 "GET /api/items" 500 34
20:29:45 "GET /api/items" 500 34
...
`
Roughly 1 in 3 requests fail — consistent with the alert's reported 31% 5xx rate.

Mechanism (traced outside-in):
frontend proxies /api/ to upstream http://10.96.149.117:8080 → Service api in namespace shop.
Service api selector is {app: api} (confirmed via kubectl get svc api -o yaml).
kubectl get endpoints api shows 3 backing pods: 10.244.1.37, 10.244.1.40, 10.244.2.48 — but Deployment api only has 2 replicas (10.244.1.37, 10.244.2.48).
The 3rd endpoint, 10.244.1.40, belongs to pod shop-api-69f6fc5964-jhzz8, from a separate Deployment shop-api. Its pod template carries labels app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api — the app: api label is a collision that causes it to be picked up by the production api Service's selector even though it's an unrelated/different service.
shop-api's code (configmap/shop-api, "shop-api 0.9.3") runs os.environ["DATABASE_URL"] on every /items request. No DATABASE_URL env var or Secret exists anywhere in the namespace (kubectl get secrets -n shop → empty), so every single request to this pod throws KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL' and returns HTTP 500 (confirmed in pod logs — the traceback repeats on every /items call, 100% failure rate for that pod).
Net effect: 1 of the 3 load-balanced endpoints behind api fails 100% of the time → ~33% error rate at the Service level, matching the alert's 31% exactly.

Ruled out:
Redis connectivity: both legitimate api pods logged connected to redis at redis:6379 and serve /items 200 consistently — no redis errors in their logs.
Node/resource exhaustion: all 3 nodes Ready; kubectl top pods shows negligible CPU/memory (1-3m CPU, <15Mi memory) across the namespace — not a capacity issue.
Frontend/nginx misconfiguration: nginx correctly proxies to the right upstream; the 502s seen at pod startup (connection refused) were transient during initial scheduling (20:28:57) and are unrelated to the ongoing 500s.

Timing: shop-api Deployment was created at 20:29:03, 9s after the core stack (api, frontend, redis) came up at 20:28:54 — this is a newly introduced, incompletely-configured service whose label collision is the proximate trigger for the alert.

VALIDATED FIXES

`text
VALIDATED FIXES:
Immediately stop shop-api from serving production "api" traffic: kubectl scale deployment shop-api -n shop --replicas=0
   Validated by: kubectl get deployment shop-api -o yaml → replicas=1, readyReplicas=1, confirmed only consumer of its traffic is the accidental inclusion in the api Service endpoints (no other Service selects it); kubectl get secrets -n shop → empty, confirming shop-api is not production-ready (missing required DATABASE_URL) and safe to pause.
   Risk: low | Undo: kubectl scale deployment shop-api -n shop --replicas=1

Permanent fix - remove the colliding app: api label so shop-api is never selected by the api Service: requires recreating/reapplying the shop-api Deployment with selector/template labels changed to e.g. app: shop-api only (Deployment selector is immutable, so this needs delete+reapply, not a patch).
   Validated by: kubectl get svc api -o yaml → selector is exactly {app: api} with no other distinguishing match; kubectl get deployment shop-api -o yaml → selector/template both include app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api. Removing app: api from both fields would exclude it from the api Service's endpoint pool.
   Risk: low (isolated to shop-api object) | Undo: reapply prior manifest with app: api label restored
`

Fix #1 is the minimum change to restore the frontend error rate to 0% right now. Fix #2 is the structural correction so this doesn't recur when shop-api is reintroduced — it should not ship with the app: api label until it's a validated replacement with its own DATABASE_URL configured and intentionally wired into the api` Service.

I'm saving this pattern to memory since the mechanism (label collision pulling an unrelated/broken deployment into a Service's endpoint pool) is non-obvious and likely to recur with other services in this cluster.

Summary

Classification: CONFIRMED

Root cause: The api Service in namespace shop selects on label app: api alone. A separate, incomplete Deployment shop-api (created 20:29:03, 9s after the core stack) carries pod template label app: api in addition to its own app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api, so its single pod got silently pulled into the api Service's endpoint pool alongside the 2 legitimate api pods. shop-api's code throws KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL' on every /items request (no such env var/secret exists in the namespace), returning HTTP 500 100% of the time for that pod. With 1 of 3 Service endpoints always broken, ~33% of frontend /api/ requests fail — matching the alert's reported 31% exactly.

Evidence trail:
nginx access logs: recurring GET /api/items -> 500 interleaved with 200s
shop-api pod logs: repeated KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL' traceback on every /items call
kubectl get endpoints api: 3 IPs vs. Deployment api's 2 replicas → 3rd IP traced to shop-api pod
kubectl get secrets -n shop: empty → DATABASE_URL never provisioned
Node/pod metrics normal (negligible CPU/mem, all nodes Ready) → ruled out resource exhaustion
Legit api pods: clean redis connections, 200s only → ruled out redis as cause

Validated fixes:
Immediate mitigation: kubectl scale deployment shop-api -n shop --replicas=0 — removes the broken pod from the Service pool. Validated: it's the sole non-conforming endpoint, no secrets wired for it, safe to pause. Low risk, reversible.
Permanent fix: Recreate shop-api Deployment without the colliding app: api label (selector is immutable, needs delete+reapply) so it's never auto-joined to the api Service.

Saved this as a learned pattern to memory (label-collision-into-Service-endpoints) since it's a non-obvious failure mode likely to recur in this fast-moving lab cluster.

## Incident Report

**HighErrorRate [warning] — namespace=shop, service=frontend**

### What Happened
At 20:29:54 on 2026-10-02, a high-severity HighErrorRate alert was triggered for the frontend service in the shop namespace [1]. Frontend nginx access logs showed repeated 500 responses on `/api/items`, interleaved with successful 200 responses, at a rate consistent with the alert's reported 31% 5xx error rate [8]. The core shop stack (frontend, api, redis) had come up at 20:28:54 [17], and the frontend pods were running normally at the infrastructure level, with no node or resource issues observed [22, 23].

### Root Cause
The root cause has been confirmed. The `api` Service in namespace shop selects pods using only the label `app: api` [17]. A separate Deployment, `shop-api`, was created at 20:29:03 — 9 seconds after the core stack came up [16] — with pod template labels `app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api` [16], causing its single pod (`shop-api-69f6fc5964-jhzz8`, IP 10.244.1.40) to be inadvertently pulled into the `api` Service's endpoint pool alongside the two legitimate `api` Deployment pods [13, 14, 18]. The `shop-api` application code calls `os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]` on every `/items` request [20], but no `DATABASE_URL` environment variable or Secret exists anywhere in the namespace [19], so every request routed to this pod throws `KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL'` and returns HTTP 500, confirmed directly in the pod's logs [15]. With 1 of the 3 load-balanced endpoints behind `api` failing 100% of the time, roughly one-third of frontend `/api/` requests fail, matching the alert's reported error rate [8, 13, 15].

### Impact & Timeline
The core stack (frontend, api, redis) was created at 20:28:54 [17]; the colliding `shop-api` Deployment was created 9 seconds later at 20:29:03 [16], and the alert fired at 20:29:54 [1]. Impact was confined to the shop namespace's `/api/items` endpoint as consumed through the frontend, with approximately 31–33% of requests to that path returning HTTP 500 for the duration of the incident [8, 13, 15]. The two legitimate `api` pods served `/items` with 200 responses throughout [10, 11].

## Ruled Out
- Redis connectivity issues — both legitimate `api` pods logged successful connections to `redis:6379` and served `/items` with 200 responses consistently [10, 11].
- Node/resource exhaustion — all nodes were in Ready state and pod CPU/memory usage was negligible (1–3m CPU, <15Mi memory) across the namespace [22, 23].
- Frontend/nginx misconfiguration — nginx logs show correct proxying behavior to the upstream `api` service, consistent with a backend-side failure rather than a routing defect [8].

## Not Checked
- The deployment/CI process that introduced the `shop-api` Deployment was not examined; only its resulting manifest and labels were inspected [16], so how or why the colliding label was introduced is not established.
- Whether other Services in the cluster have similar selector/label collision exposure was not checked; this incident is isolated to the `api` Service [17, 18].
- Historical/prior incidents involving this pattern were not found in memory, as no existing entries matched prior to this investigation [2].
